Add a facade to a tsg table

Source: R/facade.R
add_facade.Rd

This function adds a facade to a tsg table object. A facade is a set of styling options that can be applied to the table to customize its appearance. For Excel output, see openxlsx::createStyle() for all valid values.

Usage

add_facade(data, ...)

Arguments

data

A tsg table object to which the facade will be added. This is typically a data frame or tibble that has been processed using tsg functions.

...

Facade settings as part.property = value pairs, e.g. header.fontSize = 12. Valid keys are those of the default facade (see Details); an unknown key is an error. NULL values are ignored (they do not turn a setting off; use a facade file for that).

Value

A tsg object with the specified facade settings applied as attributes.

Details

Keys are part.property. The parts are table, title, subtitle, header, spanner (upper rows of a multi-level header), body, col_first, col_last, row_group, sub_group, source_note, footnotes, border_header, border_outer, border_bottom and label.

Style properties follow openxlsx::createStyle(): fontName, fontSize, fontColour, numFmt, border, borderColour, borderStyle, bgFill, fgFill, halign, valign, textDecoration, wrapText and indent. fgFill is the fill colour of a cell; bgFill is the background of an Excel fill pattern and shows only behind one (HTML and Word use it when fgFill is unset). Colours are hexadecimal codes (e.g. "#FF0000") or colour names. border is any of "top", "bottom", "left" and "right"; borderStyle uses the Excel names ("thin", "medium", "thick", "dashed", "dotted", "double", "hair", "mediumDashed", "dashDot", ...) in every output format; HTML, PDF and Word translate them to their nearest line.

The same keys style every output format. Settings that only mean something in a spreadsheet (height, width, table.offsetRow, table.offsetCol, table.gridLines, table.tabColour, table.locked, table.hidden, table.widthOffset, indent, wrapText) are ignored by HTML, PDF and Word.

Layout properties:

  • height: row height in points (border_bottom.height is the last header row of a multi-level header).

  • width: column width (table.width for all columns, col_first.width for the category column, row_group.width for grouping columns before it, col_last.width for the last). An unset (~) col_first.width or row_group.width fits the column's content.

  • table.offsetRow, table.offsetCol: rows and columns left empty before the table.

  • table.gridLines, table.tabColour, table.hidden: worksheet grid lines, tab colour and visibility.

  • table.decimalPrecision: decimal places for numeric columns with fractional values; other numbers are shown as whole numbers with thousands separators. The category and grouping columns are not formatted.

  • table.decimalCols: names of the columns to show with decimals (even when their values are whole); all other numeric columns are shown as whole numbers. The same in Excel, HTML, PDF and Word.

  • table.lastRowBold: bold last row.

  • border_outer.border: which outer sides of the table get a border, any of "top", "bottom", "left" and "right".

  • body.bandFill: fill colour of every other body row (banded rows); off by default.

  • table.widthOffset: width of the offset columns.

  • label.titleTableList, label.backHyperlink: name of the table-list sheet and text of the link back to it.

In a facade file (or a facade list passed to a writer), a key set to ~ (NULL) turns that setting off instead of falling back to the default. In add_facade() a NULL value is ignored, so it cannot turn a setting off for one table.

Use generate_template(path, "facade") to get a YAML file listing every key with its default.

Examples

person_record |>
 generate_frequency(sex) |>
 add_facade(table.offsetRow = 2, table.offsetCol = 1)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   category   frequency percent
#>   <int+lbl>      <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 1 [Male]        1516    52.0
#> 2 2 [Female]      1402    48.0
#> 3 0 [Total]       2918   100
